title: Research Fellow Tyyne Karjalainen earns Doctorate in Social Sciences
content:
FIIA Research Fellow, Master of Social Sciences Tyyne Karjalainen defended her dissertation in Political Science at the University of Turku on 20 November 2026. Karjalainen’s dissertation is titled “European joint agency in the context of Russia’s war in Ukraine: A role-theoretical analysis of the shifts in European security policies and the European Union’s enlargement policy”. It focuses on a fundamental dilemma in European external action: joint action is necessary, yet difficult to achieve. This dilemma became visible in the European response to Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022. 

Karjalainen’s dissertation applies and develops a role-theoretical framework to analyse the challenges of European joint action. It finds that

  • although the EU has collectively committed to enlargement, the process remains contested as member states, candidate countries, and external actors perform conflicting roles.

title: Finnish Institute of International Affairs launches FIIA Brussels to connect Finnish research with European policy debates
content:
As of January 2027, FIIA Brussels will host expert exchanges and policy discussions on European foreign policy, security and international affairs. 

Europe faces fundamental questions about its ability to respond to geopolitical, economic and other global challenges. To contribute to these debates, the Finnish Institute of International Affairs is bringing its broad research expertise closer to European policymaking through FIIA Brussels.  

Demand for Finnish expertise in Brussels has grown in recent years, driven by Finland’s NATO accession and the increased interest in the Nordic-Baltic region and in Finland’s comprehensive security model. FIIA Brussels provides a platform for dialogue and cooperation between Finnish and European researchers, experts and policymakers, to discuss these and other major questions facing Europe. 

“Brussels is the heart of EU, NATO and broader European policymaking. With FIIA Brussels, we want to bring our research closer to European policymakers, contribute to important debates concerning the future of Europe and strengthen the connections between European policymaking and our research in Finland,” says Niklas Helwig, Head of FIIA Brussels.

title: The Nordic-Baltic Eight policy brief: NB8 and Ukraine security cooperation
content:
New publication in the NB8 policy brief series by Olena Davlikanova (Sahaidachnyi Security Center), John Karlsrud (Norwegian Institute of International Affairs), Klara Lindström (Stockholm Centre for Eastern European Studies, Swedish Institute of International Affairs) and Lesia Ogryzko (Sahaidachnyi Security Center).

Europe’s security order is undergoing a structural transformation. The assumptions that underpinned the post-Cold War architecture – stable deterrence, US primacy and predictable threat environments – have been eroded under pressure from Russia’s protracted war against Ukraine and its broader campaign of sub-threshold operations across the continent. In this emerging landscape, Ukraine is no longer merely a recipient of security assistance. It is a central contributor to Europe’s defence capacity and a driver of its adaptation. Ukraine is also frequently mentioned when European leaders envision the future of the European security architecture – as a member of the proposed European Security Council and the European Defence Union. NB8 countries have entered into strategic partnership agreements with Ukraine and are embarking on operationalising these.

title: Parliament appoints three members to FIIA Board
content:
On 11 November 2026, the Parliament of Finland appointed three Members of Parliament as members of the institute’s Board for the term 1 Jan 2027–31 Dec 2031.

Ville Kaunisto and Vilhelm Junnila will continue as FIIA Board members. Jani Kokko was appointed as a new member.

FIIA wishes to thank MP Kimmo Kiljunen whose term in the Board now comes to an end and bids the new members warmly welcome to the institute’s Board.

title: FIIA is seeking two researchers
content:
The Finnish Institute of International Affairs is seeking researchers for two-year fixed-term positions. The positions are in two research programmes, with one vacancy in each programme.

Finland and Northern European Security research programme

The regional focus of the programme is Finland’s immediate security environment, developments in which have direct implications for Finland’s national security. The programme broadly monitors various aspects of Finland’s foreign, security, and defence policy, including Finland’s relations with major powers, its military cooperation, NATO’s activities, and the development of NATO’s defence and deterrence posture (including nuclear deterrence), Nordic cooperation, and Russia’s foreign, security, and defence policy in relation to Finland. The thematic scope of the research also includes Finland’s security of supply, national resilience policy, and issues related to the comprehensive security approach.

title: The Nordic-Baltic Eight policy brief: China’s green statecraft and NB8 Arctic security
content:
New publication in the NB8 policy brief series by Dana Dūda (LIIA), Konstantinas Andrijauskas (IIRPS VU) and Björn Cappelin (UI).

Energy dependence has become a geopolitical liability. Russia’s war against Ukraine, the US-Iran war and tensions with the Kingdom of Denmark over Greenland have all exposed the strategic weight of energy independence, critical minerals, and Arctic access. For the eight Nordic-Baltic states (NB8), the next vulnerability may emerge from the green transition itself, where China’s dominance in clean technologies and critical mineral processing can be converted into strategic leverage. Some dependence is unavoidable in the short term; the task is to manage it deliberately rather than let it accumulate by default. This policy brief argues for integrating green energy security and Arctic security within a one strategic framework, because the Arctic’s critical mineral resources, renewable energy infrastructure and emerging transport and digital connectivity projects are relevant to Europe’s efforts to strengthen its energy dependence. This brief proposes collective measures to limit strategic dependence on China in the long term.

title: Report: Climate risks could multiply disruptions to Finland’s security of supply
content:
Climate change threatens Finland’s security of supply by increasing the likelihood of simultaneous crises and disruptions. Finland must prepare for climate risks as part of geopolitical crises and security policy, states a new report by the Finnish Institute of International Affairs (FIIA) and the National Emergency Supply Agency (NESA).

“Climate risks cannot be treated as something that we can circle back to once military crises are over,” says Leading Researcher Emma Hakala from FIIA, who headed the research project.

For example, extreme weather events can disrupt production, transport and the supply of critical raw materials, all of which are essential for security of supply, while the very same supply chains are being hindered by wars and trade disputes.

“This year, heatwaves caused significant problems across Europe, and the impacts of such phenomena are also quickly felt in Finland,” Hakala points out.

title: The Nordic-Baltic Eight policy brief: NB8 and the drone challenge
content:
New publication in the NB8 policy brief series by Justinas Lingevicius (VU IIRPS) and Markus Holmgren (FIIA).

Drone incursions in the Baltic States and Finland have made clear that this is no longer a distant battlefield concern. This brief argues that as the NB8 framework matures into an increasingly like-minded security community, drone cooperation could stimulate market integration. A standardised, modular drone platform architecture, a European drone defence “Platform market” model, could give the countries the economy of scale that they otherwise lack.

This policy brief series aims to deepen understanding of the evolving security, political, and societal dynamics that shape the Nordic-Baltic region amid renewed great-power competition.

title: The era of single-solution security is over: Helsinki Security Forum 2026 explores new layers of security
content:
The era of single-solution security is over. In a world shaped by disruption and competition, resilience no longer stems from a single security guarantee, alliance, or strategy.

The fifth annual Helsinki Security Forum (HSF) will take place in Helsinki on 2–4 October 2026, bringing together international policymakers and experts to discuss the future of Finnish and European security. The theme of HSF 2026, Layers of Security, highlights both the different layers of security and the diverse actors who help shape them.

“European security is being shaped simultaneously by geopolitical, technological and economic competition, as well as a changing climate. Security is built across multiple layers and by a wide range of actors. Europe must strengthen its ability to act across all these levels if it wants to shape its own security in an increasingly competitive world,” says Hiski Haukkala, Director of the Finnish Institute of International Affairs.
